_readme: Review Removal page (/review-removal/). Copy from Len's Launch Brief, Part 2, with Andy's edits (Oct 15, 2026). Every button opens the intake form. Testimonial screenshots are hotlinked from Len's HighLevel media library (same images as thereviewsdoctor.com).

seo.pageTitle: Google Review Removal for Dentists | Dr. Len Tau, The Reviews Doctor
seo.description: Remove fake and policy-violating Google reviews from your dental practice. Pay $450 only if the review comes down. No upfront cost.

hero.title: Bad Google review? You pay only if it comes down.
hero.text: Some reviews break Google's rules. Fake patients. Former employees. Competitors. I get those reviews in front of Google the right way. You pay $450 per review, only when it's removed.
hero.note: No charge until a review is removed.

problem.title: Flagging it yourself rarely works.
paragraphs: You reported the review. Weeks passed. Nothing happened.
You posted a calm reply. The 1-star still sits at the top of your profile.
You priced reputation agencies. They wanted $2,000 to $5,000 a month with no promise of removal.
The review is still there. New patients read it before they call.

how.title: Three steps. | Two minutes of your time.

steps.title: Submit your review links.
steps.text: The form takes about two minutes.

steps.title: We submit to Google.
steps.text: We start within 24 hours. If Google removes the review, you pay $450. If not, you pay nothing.

qualifies.title: Respond to the real ones. | Remove the ones that break Google's rules.

yes.title: Reviews Google may remove
items: From someone who was never a patient
From a current or former employee
Containing hate speech, threats, or personal information
Off-topic, spam, or posted for the wrong business

no.title: Reviews Google will not remove
items: An honest negative review from a real patient
no.text: For those, reply in a calm, professional voice. The next patient is reading your response.

pricing.title: One price. | Only if it works.
paragraphs: Your card is stored through Stripe. It is charged only when Google removes a review. About 4 in 10 reviews stay up. You pay nothing for those.
No retainer. No contract. No monthly fee.

items.a: You submit your review links through our form. My team prepares each submission and sends it to Google. If Google removes the review, your card is charged $450. If it stays up, you pay nothing.

items.q: Why do I need a card on file?
items.a: Stripe stores it securely so we can charge you only after a removal. Nothing is charged at submission. If no review comes down, we never charge your card.
About 60%. Roughly 4 of every 10 reviews stay up. You pay zero for those.

items.q: Can you remove any negative review?
items.a: No. Google removes reviews that break its policies. An honest review from a real patient stays up.
We start within 24 hours. Google sets the timeline. Some reviews come down in days. Others take weeks. You hear from us the moment Google decides.

items.q: What if new negative reviews show up later?
items.a: Submit them anytime. Same terms. Most practices come back monthly.

cta.title: Your profile should show | the practice you run.
cta.text: Submit your reviews today. You pay only when one comes down.
